rationale: The Hercules dSph density-profile normalisation rho_s is attributed via the table caption to \cite{Albert, lat}; the original value 23988329 M_sun/kpc^3 corresponds to log10(rho_s)=7.380, consistent with the HAWC/HESS-type analyses cited. The perturbed value 35481339 corresponds to log10(rho_s)=7.550, a shift of +0.17 dex. Typical kinematic uncertainties on log10(rho_s) for ultra-faint dSphs in these references are sigma~0.10-0.15 dex, putting this perturbation in the 1.1-1.7 sigma window — definitively outside 1 sigma but well within 2 sigma. Cite key intact, surrounding row entries (coords, distance, R_Delta, r_s) untouched. Caveat: this paper genuinely has thin pickings for citations-S1-type-2 because the authors rarely quote 'value +/- sigma' from cited literature in prose; the table value attributed to \cite{Albert} is the most defensible quantitative-qualifier-attached-to-cite target available, though it is a table entry rather than a free-prose claim sentence.
ground_truth_description: In the dSphs parameter table (results.tex), the Hercules density-profile normalisation rho_s was perturbed from 23988329 to 35481339 M_sun/kpc^3 (log10 7.38 -> 7.55, a +0.17 dex shift, roughly 1.1-1.7 sigma relative to typical reported uncertainties), while the citation \cite{Albert, lat} attributing this value remains untouched.

rationale: The conformal factor Omega^2 is defined generally as Omega^2(varphi,X)=1+2 kappa^2 xi F(varphi,X) and then specialised, for F linear in phi with proportionality M, to Omega^2(phi)=1+2 xi M kappa^2 phi; doubling the linear coefficient in the specialised form makes the two displayed definitions disagree on Omega^2 (and on the subsequent Taylor-expansion that uses 2 xi M kappa^2 phi), giving a within-paper cross-equation inconsistency for an S1 mathematics target.
ground_truth_description: In the specialised conformal factor Omega^2(phi) = 1 + 2 xi M kappa^2 phi, the linear coefficient was changed from 2 to 4, contradicting the general definition Omega^2(varphi,X) = 1 + 2 kappa^2 xi F(varphi,X) under the linear ansatz F ~ M phi used in the paper.
